memory_versions.text:
Order intake notes

- Form version 1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Extract the complete JSON from the source text; do not rely on truncated previews. Preserve valid values exactly.
- Rejections commonly involve missing/invalid priority and ship_country; qty may also need correction. Validate all six fields before submitting.
- On retry, retain already-valid cust, email, and order_date, and repair only the fields listed as invalid. Successful retries (ORD-5104, ORD-5106, ORD-5108) show that correcting the bad fields works.
- Do not resubmit an unchanged record: ORD-5100 failed all three attempts and went to manual review.
- Attempt limits are three per order. Use the first rejection to identify fields needing repair; ensure the next submission is complete and valid.
- Customer/source wording can vary (handwritten, phone, voicemail, email, portal), but extract the structured order data rather than copying surrounding narrative.

Order intake notes

- Form version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 2 has so far shown the same field list, but verify its schema before processing.
- Extract the complete JSON from the source record, not truncated previews or surrounding narrative. Preserve valid values exactly.
- Validate all required fields before each submission, especially priority, ship_country, and qty. Front-desk statements such as “ordinary priority” do not prove the encoded value is valid.
- On retry, retain already-valid cust, email, and order_date; repair every field listed as invalid. Do not fix only one issue when multiple invalid fields remain.
- A prior rejection does not necessarily identify all fields that must be repaired: later attempts may expose additional invalid fields. Revalidate the full six-field record before resubmitting.
- Do not resubmit an unchanged record. Successful retries (ORD-5104, ORD-5106, ORD-5108, ORD-5110, ORD-5112) confirm that complete correction works.
- Attempt limit is three per order. Use the first rejection to plan a complete valid retry; after the third failed attempt, the record goes to manual review.
- ORD-5115 and ORD-5118 reached manual review after repeated incomplete/incorrect repairs, reinforcing the need to correct all invalid fields at once.
- Customer/source wording varies (handwritten, phone, voicemail, email, portal); extract structured order data rather than copying narrative.
- Duplicate-check statements indicate intake status only; still process the supplied order data and schema normally.

Order intake notes

- Form versions 1 and 2 both use exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 2 is now confirmed, but verify schema if a new version appears.
- Extract the complete JSON from the source record, not truncated previews or surrounding narrative. Preserve valid values exactly; do not copy narrative wording into structured fields.
- Validate all six fields before every submission, especially priority, ship_country, and qty. Front-desk descriptions such as “ordinary priority” do not establish a valid encoded value.
- A rejection may identify only some invalid fields. On every retry, revalidate the entire record and repair all invalid fields at once, while retaining already-valid cust, email, and order_date.
- Do not resubmit an unchanged record or assume the prior rejection was exhaustive. ORD-5127 through ORD-5129 showed different invalid fields across retries; fixing one field alone still failed and led to manual review.
- Attempt limit is three per order. Plan a complete valid correction after the first rejection; after the third failed attempt, the record goes to manual review. ORD-5115, ORD-5118, and ORD-5129 reinforce this.
- Successful complete corrections (ORD-5104, ORD-5106, ORD-5108, ORD-5110, ORD-5112, ORD-5120, ORD-5122, ORD-5124, ORD-5126) confirm that full-record repair works.
- Customer/source wording varies (handwritten, phone, voicemail, email, portal); always extract structured order data.
- Duplicate-check statements indicate intake status only. Process the supplied order and schema normally.

Order intake notes

- Versions 1, 2, and 3 currently use six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Verify the schema whenever a new version appears.
- Extract the complete JSON from the source record, not truncated previews or surrounding narrative. Preserve valid values exactly; never infer structured values from front-desk wording.
- Validate all six fields before every submission, especially priority, qty, and ship_country. Descriptions such as “ordinary priority” do not establish a valid encoded value.
- A rejection may name only some invalid fields. Revalidate the entire record on every retry and repair every invalid field together, while retaining already-valid cust, email, and order_date.
- Never resubmit an unchanged record or assume a rejection was exhaustive. Recent batches again showed priority, qty, and ship_country errors appearing across successive attempts.
- There are three attempts per order. Plan a complete correction after the first rejection; after the third failure, the record goes to manual review. ORD-5129, ORD-5130, and ORD-5133–5135 confirm this.
- Full-record repair can succeed: ORD-5136/5137 was accepted on attempt 2 after correcting the rejected fields. Prior successful corrections likewise confirm this approach.
- Customer/source wording varies (handwritten, phone, voicemail, email, portal); always extract structured order data from the source.
- Duplicate-check statements indicate intake status only. Process the supplied order and schema normally.
